_doc: Declares this repo's legal/consent surfaces per cais-shared-services/REGULATORY_INCLUSIONS.md. Every inclusion must be default, customised, or not-applicable WITH A REASON — silence is not acceptance.

operator._doc: Trigger A. Kira is a CAS-owned product, so it carries OUR canonical identity (portfolio-manifest.yaml `shared:`). A white-label or distributor product would carry theirs — that is the gate, and this is the case where the default is correct rather than assumed.

review._doc: Best-fit pages written from what the product actually does. Not legal advice — the same standing caveat lib/terms.ts already carries.
review.note: A lawyer should review before real volume, together with the introducer agreement (BROKER_CHANNEL_BUILD_STATE guardrails). Not blocking today: Kira is CAS-owned, so unlike BucketLyst there is no third party whose entity we are guessing at.

privacy.note: lib/privacy.ts, mirroring lib/terms.ts so the two versions and dates can be reasoned about together. Three sections that could not have come from a template: what an INTRODUCER can see (status only — enforced by introducer_owner_projection in SQL, so it is stated as fact not promise), what Kira remembers (distilled summary, per-account, deletable without closing the account), and the valuation figures (turnover and profit, collected before an account even exists).

terms.note: lib/terms.ts. Version recorded at signup acceptance, so it is answerable which wording a given user agreed to.

voice.note: Vendor consent modal (ElevenLabs), unmodified. The package exposes NO consent-text configuration, so overriding it needs a direct API PATCH or a package addition. Mitigated by privacy §4, which states the same thing in our words. The naive-tester finding was that product copy CONTRADICTED the modal ('what you tell Kira stays between you and your business'); the privacy policy now reconciles it — the data stays with the account, and the processing by ElevenLabs is stated plainly rather than left to the vendor notice alone.

ip_ack.reason: Users do not create or share content built on third-party IP. What they produce is their own business information, and the terms already state it remains theirs.

cookies.reason: Session cookie only, strictly necessary to keep a signed-in user signed in. No analytics, no advertising, no cross-site tracking — disclosed in the privacy policy rather than gated behind a banner. Re-declare the moment any analytics is added.

sender.note: Canonical CAS identity via @caistech/email-compliance senderFromEnv(); assertCompliant() throws on a commercial send missing ABN or unsubscribe. EMAIL_SENDER_* are set in Vercel.
